description: We are students from Wesley girls  high school in Ghana representing PRAIX .
summary: STARBOUND is a browser-based space mission game where the player carries out every step of a mission instead of watching it. Players walk through a space centre, climb into the spacecraft, flip the launch switches, float through zero gravity, steer past hazards, land by hand, collect samples and walk home. There are four missions: finding a hidden world in a dimming star’s light curve, searching the Moon for a silent probe, finding ice in a Mercury crater, and listening for a signal under Europa’s ice. A friendly guide, PIP, gives hints and reads the stories aloud, and players choose Guided, Standard or Independent help. Early testers told us games that run the mission for you are boring, so we made every step the player’s own. STARBOUND teaches how a real mission is put together, and how to say only what the evidence supports. It matters because space missions feel far away to many young people; carrying one out makes the science and engineering behind exploration personal and memorable. It runs in a web browser with nothing to install.
details:
• STARBOUND lets players run a whole space mission by hand, from checking in at a space centre to assembling probes and satellites then launching them in outer space yourself. Each of the six missions opens with a short story and ends with a result screen. The Exoplanet Transit Watcher, Flood Mapper, Wildfire Spotter, Asteroid Hunter, Hurricane Spotter and Solar Wind Sentinel share the same hands-on steps with a different world, sky, gravity, samples and ending.The game is made with Three.js and JavaScript, and its 3D scenes, characters and sounds are generated in code. Every action is something the player does: building the satellites, climbing the ladder, flipping switches, steering past asteroids, and taking photos. PIP guides the player with an arrow and a marker, and reads stories and crew lines aloud.
  • STARBOUND helps players understand how a real space mission fits together by letting them do each step themselves. They learn what every part of a spacecraft does, why it is tested before launch, and the physics that gets a rocket to orbit. A guide explains each part out loud, and a Hint button always shows the next move. Players also practise saying only what their evidence supports. Three assist levels suit different players, whether they play solo or with a team, and the game runs in a web browser, including on a phone, with nothing to install.
  • As a team, we want space exploration to feel like something young people can do, not just watch, we want them to have an almost realistic feel of the preparations that go on before an astronaut is able to board the rocket ship and also a little bit of what happens in outer space. Early testers told us games that run the mission for you are boring, so we rebuilt every step as the player’s own.
  • JavaScript, HTML, CSS and Three.js, bundled with esbuild and tested with browser play-throughs. We used GitHub for the code and Vercel for hosting, and tested the game on a phone browser. We built it with help from Claude for coding and tests and documentation directed by our team’s design and feedback.
  • You aren't just picking options from a menu—you walk into the STARBOUND center, carry parts to the stand, torque bolts in a star pattern, stack a two-stage rocket, walk 80 metres up the launch tower arm with your crew, and fly the mission yourself also having PIP the robot alongside team guides (Godiva, Lady Paula, Afia, and Jehielle) explain parts out loud—plus built-in tools like exploded view, X-ray, and hints—keeps learning conversational and approachable
